vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

findings.value: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant identified
One non-cysteine-altering variant of uncertain significance, c.3058G>A p.(Ala1020Thr) — not the CADASIL mechanism
CADASIL not supported: the pathogenic mechanism is cysteine-altering variants in EGF-like repeats 1-34, and none is present

output.impression: No pathogenic NOTCH3 variant. The single variant of uncertain significance is non-cysteine-altering and is not the mechanism of CADASIL, so it must not be reported to the patient as a diagnosis. Hereditary arteriopathy is not supported, and the severe burden is attributable to sixteen years of poorly controlled severe hypertension with stimulant use, untreated sleep apnoea, smoking, dyslipidaemia and hyperhomocysteinaemia.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not report a non-cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant of uncertain significance as CADASIL, and do not offer relatives cascade testing on that basis
Do not treat the severity of the imaging as proof of a hereditary disease when the acquired burden is this large
Do not lower blood pressure abruptly in a patient with severe small-vessel disease and grade 3 retinopathy; titrate with renal monitoring
Do not stop investigating the acquired causes because a genetic test has been sent
Do not prescribe sympathomimetics or stimulants
required_recommendations: Recognise that a severe burden before 60 requires either a hereditary explanation or an exceptional acquired one, and quantify the acquired one before assuming the first
Look specifically for anterior temporal pole and U-fibre involvement, whose absence argues against CADASIL
Exclude the acquired causes of premature small-vessel disease and quantify those that are present
Send NOTCH3 sequencing given the age and the family history, and interpret a variant of uncertain significance correctly rather than as a diagnosis
Document end-organ damage in the eye and kidney, which corroborates the severity and the duration of the hypertension
Treat every acquired driver, with adherence as the central problem
Deliver the CPAP that was prescribed four years ago and never collected

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

accepted: Vascular dementia — severe premature sporadic cerebral small-vessel disease from sixteen years of poorly controlled severe hypertension with stimulant use, untreated obstructive sleep apnoea, smoking, dyslipidaemia and hyperhomocysteinaemia; CADASIL excluded

differential.key_features: Sixteen years of severe poorly treated hypertension with grade 3 retinopathy, macroalbuminuria and left ventricular hypertrophy, and an imaging signature that matches — this is the diagnosis

Age 54, a severe burden and a father who died of stroke at 55 make it a necessary test, but the anterior temporal poles and U-fibres are spared, there is no migraine, there is no multigenerational pattern, and NOTCH3 sequencing found no pathogenic variant
Stimulant use accelerates small-vessel disease and contributes here; it is part of the acquired burden rather than a separate diagnosis, and it has stopped
Sixty grams daily is a contributor worth addressing, but there is no Korsakoff phenotype and no cerebellar atrophy, and the imaging is a hypertensive arteriopathy
All five microbleeds are deep or infratentorial with no lobar lesion or siderosis, and the patient is 54

key_clinical_evidence: Premature small-vessel disease has two possible explanations and they are not mutually exclusive to test: a hereditary arteriopathy, or an acquired burden severe enough to produce the same picture two decades early — and this patient's acquired burden is quantifiable in five organs

The imaging carries the discrimination: symmetric anterior temporal pole and U-fibre involvement is the CADASIL marker, and its absence with severe basal-ganglia perivascular spaces and deep microbleeds is the hypertensive signature
A negative genetic test is a positive result here: it redirects the entire management toward the acquired drivers, all of which are treatable, whereas CADASIL is not
Variants of uncertain significance cause harm when reported as diagnoses — a non-cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant is not CADASIL, and telling this family otherwise would create false hereditary risk
Grade 3 retinopathy and macroalbuminuria date the hypertension and corroborate that the brain damage is hypertensive, which no single blood-pressure reading could do

labs.interpretation: The acquired burden is heavy and quantified: LDL 158 mg/dL, HDL 32 mg/dL, triglycerides 268 mg/dL, HbA1c 6.3%, homocysteine 18.6 umol/L, creatinine 1.42 with eGFR 54 and macroalbuminuria at 148 mg/g, and a haematocrit of 47.8% in a heavy smoker with untreated sleep apnoea. Inflammatory markers and antiphospholipid antibodies are negative. Every one of these is an acquired driver of premature small-vessel disease.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Danilo Rossetti is a 54-year-old self-employed builder who attends with his partner, unable to work for the past year. She describes three years of progressive change: he cannot plan a job, has lost customers by failing to quote or invoice, forgets what he has been told unless reminded of the setting, and has become slow and apathetic. Walking changed eighteen months ago, with small steps and one fall. He was diagnosed with hypertension at 38 and has been in and out of treatment ever since, with a recorded 190/110 three years ago and 186/108 today on two agents that he takes irregularly. He used cocaine intermittently from his late twenties until two years ago. He was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnoea four years ago and never collected the CPAP machine. He smokes thirty cigarettes a day and drinks about sixty grams of ethanol daily. His father died at 55 of a stroke and also had untreated hypertension; there is no pattern of early dementia across generations, and his mother is well at 79. He has never had migraine. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation and no dream enactment.

neurological_exam.additional: Frontal release signs present. Blood pressure 186/108 at this visit on two agents. No stigmata of chronic liver disease.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundi show grade 3 hypertensive retinopathy with flame haemorrhages and exudates. Visual fields full. Speech mildly dysarthric.
neurological_exam.gait: Short-stepped, wide-based, low clearance, arm swing preserved. Tandem impossible. One fall.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, year correct, month incorrect. MoCA 19/30 with education-adjusted interpretation, losing points on trail-making, cube, clock, digit span, serial sevens, fluency (7 animals) and delayed recall (2/5 unaided, 4/5 cued).
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Increased tone in both legs. Strength 5/5 with 4+/5 hip flexion bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ knees, 3+ ankles, plantar responses extensor bilaterally.
